1.1: Nahum pop up on the scene like, "I got a word for Nineveh." That's the same city God had mercy on in Jonah's day… but this time? Mercy expired.
1.2: God jealous—not petty, but protective. He don't let evil just slide.
1.3: He slow to pop off, but when He do? It's justice time. The same God who run storms and moves mountains got receipts. Ain't no wickedness slipping past Him.
1.4: When He show up, nature itself trembles—seas dry, mountains melt, valleys split.
1.6: Who gon' stand when He bring the heat? Nobody. Period.
1.7: But if you His? You good. He know who really trustin' Him. He a safe spot when life go left.
1.8: Enemies of God? They done. Don't care how deep you hide or how tough you act—He clearing 'em out.
1.11: That wicked counselor? Yeah, he gon' get exposed and buried.
1.12: God say, "I know you been through it. But I'm takin' the weight off. That yoke? I'm breakin' it. Those chains? Snappin' 'em."
1.14: For Nineveh, it's a wrap. False gods? Gone. Legacy? Buried. They had a good run—but judgment day done pulled up.
1.15: And now? God say, "Celebrate, Judah! You free." Peace finally got real estate. The wicked? They ain't comin' back.

2.1: God say, "Ayo Nineveh, somebody comin' for you." This ain't no sneak attack either—He givin' y'all the play-by-play: Get ready… not that it'll help.
2.2: God ain't forgot His people. Even though Israel got stripped and trampled, He gon' restore what was stolen. The vine gon' grow again.
2.3: The scene look like a Fast & Furious movie—chariots flashin', swords gleamin', soldiers suited up like it's game time. It's chaos. War on sight.
2.5: Even the leaders stumbling around, tryin' to get in position, but it's too late. The city's defenses fallin' apart—rivers overflowin', palace crumblin' like it's made of sand.
2.7: Queen gettin' dragged out. The people fleein' like water spillin' from a cup. "Stop, come back!" But they out—they ain't loyal to the empire, they scared.
2.9: All that gold? That silver? That luxury they stashed up from oppressin' others? Gone. Wiped out. City empty. Hearts droppin', faces pale. Karma hit like a freight train.
2.11: God mockin' them like, "Where them lion dens now?" Y'all used to devour nations, take what you wanted, walk around like you untouchable. Now you food.
2.13: Final nail: "I'm against you," says God. Not your haters. Not your enemies. God. And when He against you? It's over. Your army? Done. Your rep? Dead. Your messengers? Silenced.

3.1: "Woe to the bloody city!" Off top, Nineveh gettin' exposed. This city built off lies, robberies, and violence. And guess what? God seen all of it. The victims never stopped sufferin', but now it's time for the empire to pay up.
3.2: Picture it: whips crackin', wheels spinnin', swords flashin'. Horses gallopin', chariots clankin'. Bodies everywhere. Folks trippin' over corpses. This ain't no metaphor—it's a massacre. Ain't no pride left in power when God turn the tables.
3.4: And why is all this happenin'? 'Cause Nineveh was out here seducin' nations with sorcery, playin' the harlot with their influence. They had folks under a spell—economically, politically, spiritually. God like, "You was out here pimpin' nations and families? Bet."
3.5: God say, "I'm exposin' you." And not metaphorically. Skirts lifted, shame on full display. You gon' be made an example. Nations gon' look at you and keep it movin'—ain't nobody cryin' for you now. You was the bully, and now you laid out.
3.8: God pull up history receipts: "You think you better than Thebes (No Amon)?" That city had allies, water defenses, and still got wiped out. Babies smashed, leaders enslaved. And you? You next.
3.11: Nineveh drunk now—not off wine, but off fear. No more soldiers, just soft hands and shaky knees. Gates wide open, defenses burnt up. You was talkin' tough—now you lookin' like lunch.
3.14: "Go ahead, try to prep for battle." Make bricks. Draw water. Gear up. Do all that… it won't matter. Fire and sword still gon' eat you alive. You can multiply like locusts, but you still gettin' dealt with.
3.16: God say, "Y'all had merchants, captains, leaders—all stacked up like stars." But they scatterin' now. Fleein' when the heat come. Ain't no loyalty in fake power. Just folks runnin' when the bag disappear.
3.18: God speak directly to the king of Assyria: "Your people scattered, your nobles sleepin', and your wound? Fatal. Ain't no comeback story." And the coldest part? The whole world clappin' when they hear you fell. That's how hated Nineveh was. Ain't nobody mournin'. Everyone relieved.
